title: Introduce safety-normalized quant profiles and adaptive batch defaults
author: Maya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers with strict output-quality contracts were seeing silent regressions when aggressive quant profiles and batch heuristics were applied. This PR implements a safety-normalized quant profile generator plus an adaptive batch defaults controller that biases for cost while keeping a lightweight continuous QA probe to guard against quality regressions.

What this changes: generates candidate quantization profiles normalized by a safety floor (measured on a small labeled prompt set) and ships an adaptive suggestion pipeline that adjusts batch_size and cache hints per model+workload fingerprint. The system produces human-readable scoring, expected cost delta, and rollback triggers tied to quality thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] quant profile generator (Python) with CI unit tests
- [x] runtime hooks for applying profile metadata at model load (Go)
- [x] adaptive batch defaults controller with workload fingerprinting (Rust service)
- [x] lightweight evaluation probe that runs continuous micro-evals against canary traffic
- [x] docs and console suggestions plumbing
- [x] safety rollback path + monitoring alerts

Related: Linear ENG-4321 (quant safety baseline), ENG-4390 (adaptive batching pilot). Also references design notes: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4321/quant-safety-baseline and a small internal spec: docs/design/safety-normalized-quant.md.

Summary of work:
- Adds a profile tuning pipeline (optimize/quant_profile_tuner.py) which scores candidate quant matrices by: (1) expected compute delta, (2) loss in rerank/LL metrics on eval set, (3) a safety-normalized penalty if metric loss exceeds a small epsilon. This produces profiles annotated with "safety_score" and "expected_cost_savings".
- Adds runtime flagging to model metadata and a deterministic application path in serving/runtime/loader.go so Dedicated and Private deployments can pin or accept suggested profiles.
- Introduces an adaptive batch defaults service (scheduler/batch_advisor.rs) that watches windowed latency/coldstart stats and suggests per-route batch_size/cache_ttl defaults to console via the suggestions API.
- Adds a canary micro-eval harness (evals/micro_probe.py) that runs a 20-sample prompt set against suggested profile+batch combo and emits a quality delta. The controller uses the probe to automatically reject suggestions that exceed the safety threshold.

Commit summary: see commit_summaries field.

Files changed (high level): serving/runtime/loader.go, serving/runtime/batcher.go, optimize/quant_profile_tuner.py, scheduler/batch_advisor.rs, evals/micro_probe.py, console/api/suggestions.rs, docs/design/safety-normalized-quant.md, tests/quant_tuner_test.py, tests/micro_probe_integration.sh

CI and checks: pipeline runs include unit, integration, and smoke benchmarks. One intermittent performance flaky in the scheduler integration (rust test) was fixed by reducing a synthetic timeout. All checks passed on final run.

Merge rationale: combines safety-first quant recommendations (preventing silent quality regressions) with an automated, observable batching suggestion pipeline that reduces unit cost for the common case while providing safe rollback. This is intended as an opt-in suggestions feature for Hosted and an opt-in default for Dedicated trials.

review_conversation:
Reviewer: Evan Cheng: Can you clarify how the safety-normalized penalty is computed? Also request stronger integration test coverage for large-sequence scenarios.
Author (Maya): @Evan the penalty is a multiplicative term that scales linearly when metric loss > epsilon; details in docs/design/safety-normalized-quant.md (section 3). I added a new integration that runs a sampled long-seq profile to tests/micro_probe_integration.sh.
Reviewer: Priya Nair: The console suggestions look noisy for very low-volume routes, can the advisor suppress suggestions below a min-op threshold?
Author: added a min_request_threshold config and a suppress_until window for routes with < 100 requests in 24h.
Reviewer: Carlos Ruiz: Did you consider tying the probe to the existing evals infra so we reuse golden prompt sets?
Author: yes — the probe uses a compact golden set indexed under evals/golden/mini_probe_v1.txt and is configurable; I included a migration note for later consolidation.
Reviewer: QA (Lena): Where are the rollback alerts wired?
Author: alert rules live in observability/alerts/quant-safety.rules and console will show rejected suggestions with reasons (safety_score/exceeded_delta).

- Evan Cheng: APPROVED after comments addressed

release_notes: Adds safety-normalized quant profile generation and an adaptive batch defaults suggestion service. Opt-in for Hosted; optional for Dedicated trials. Includes automatic rollback when micro-eval safety thresholds are violated.
